questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was drawn towards the city of Vienna due to its history and always its impact on my subject field, Psychology. Furthermore the academic profile of the host university appealed to me - prioritizing perspectives of psychoanalysis and social science. It was always crucial to not travel too far from my home country Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic experience of the host university was very poor, and i felt understimulated compared to university of Copenhagen. I will elaborate further on this below. Besides this, the opportunity to travel abroad - with funding - and have time to experience the culture and history of the city has been very meaningful to me.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I am unsure of which information is reffered to. I had beforehand found accomodation indenpendently of the university, and did not require specific assistent in regards to arriving in the city. Besides this, the university was helpful to send out in information about study start, course enrollment and so on.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got a orientation letter from the host university, explaining the basic logistics of arriving in the city. The information was very helpful in regards to transportation, visa and so on.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it relatively easy. I searched both on Facebook and in the app WG-gesucht. I would reccomend to start looking at least 1,5 month before. Wg-gesucht is great if you want to live in a shared flat, with other young people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a good way to meet other people, that is not attending your specific study. I think it is a wonderful way experience something else that the sphere around the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I cannot answer this competently, as i did not use the housing for students that might have been provided by the university.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was overall confusion in regards to the course registratin. Eventually it worked out fine though. But i wanted to attend courses from different faculties, and i was told that it would be possible. But because of administration issues the course catalogue of the Psychotherapy Faculty was not complete until the third week of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a study service center, and they where very helpful to assist me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Eventually i was succesful and everything worked out fine in regards to course registration.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont expect to have a complete schedule on the first day of the semester. There will most likely be overlaps and cancellation of courses, which will cause you to "re-plan" your studies a little bit. Trust that this will work out eventually. The issue of "getting the course first" didnt seem to be a problem at SFU, as it seems at other universities. I got all the courses, that where mandatory for me (from KU), which where the most important.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The academic level overall, was surprisingly low. Unclear if this was due to teaching or student environment, but probably both. In most classes (not all) there existed a culture of discussing with personal anecdotes and opinions without connecting it to scientific litterature. It was my experience that most of the teachers often where unable to make these connections. In Psychological Diagnostics a youtube video from a influencer psychologist was presented in order to show how a therapy session should start and end. No scientific discussion followed. Claims about the scientific value of many psychological paradigms (eg psychoanalysis) where often dismissed as unscientific, without proper argumentation.
Many teachers presented subject matter without references. In clinical psychology it was obvious that the lecture slides was AI generated. Here the teacher highly encouraged the students to "share" what diagnoses they had. I found it unethical and unscientific.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Different. Lectures and seminar classes where often "integrated" meaning that the same teacher stood in front of the class for 3-4 hours. It was often unclear when we should work with texts ourselves and when the "lecture part" was going on. It was very unstructurered, and combined with VERY strict attending requirements, i felt this had a bad effect on student participation and thriving.  

Coming from UCPH it was a culture chok. I would not recommend other students to go on exchange at SFU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Grocery prices where pretty high. Also, now Vienna has taken away the "semester" ticket for public transportation, so expect to pay a little more. 
Also when you go through the "meldephlicht", you have to pay 20-50 euro to "register" in the city.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Prices of groceries where high. 
The rent of living was low, at least compared to my home town of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had to find it elsewhere, primarily at the Universitat Wien

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was probably some, but i did not find them. In the beginning of the semester i asked to join the universities football team, but they did not have any. I instead found a team through the main university of Vienna.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I am sorry but i cannot be helpful here, because i did not attend anything. I am aware of the "SFU-ball" in the winter, which might be fun. Besidses this the university hosts guests and talks regularly, but most where in German, so i did not go.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to the sorounding capital cities, they are close by.  There is wonderfull nature around the city of Wien, go on hikes or swim in the Donau. You can also take the train to the alps, and hike for the weekend. 
Make use of the many cultural offers in the city, it is really remarkable.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
It was pretty easy, as i experienced the viennese simularly to the copenhagen people i am used to. 
Dont eat or talk on the phone in public transportation. The locals dont appreciate it.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Make use of the "USI" which is the sports catalogue for students in Vienna. Here you can attend everything from football to salsa to thaiboxing. It is a GREAT way to meet other people/students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Soimetimes the viennese can come across as unpolite. You have to get use to this. Most are happy to talk, but can seem unfriendly in the beginning. This is similar to Copenhagen, so i found it not so difficult.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Vienna is a culture city, and there is really always something to experience. I bought both the NONSTOP abonnoment that gives unlimited access to all cinema showings in Wien for 22euro/month. Wien has beautifull cinemas and often niche themes and showings. 
Besides this i bought the bundeskart that gives access to all the major museums for 99euro/year, i found this very nice, as a single entrance ticket often amounts to 14/15 euros. If you like museums, then this offer is very good.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Dont expect a buzzing student environment. SFU is a small university. There is close to non common areas, which makes it difficult to "enter" into the student environment. The student unions or communities, if there are any, are not visible. 
Also expect the attendance requirement culture to be very different from UCPH. At SFU, everything besides lectures, has an 80% attendance, and you need a doctors note. 
There is no reading hall at the university, so if you appreciate this, then find it in the city: there is plenty. TU at Karlsplatz, Kunstakademi Schillerplatz and the uni Wien at Spitalgasse.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Make use of the study service center as much as you can. 
Also, if you come from UCPH, expect a different exam period. At SFU you will have maybe 8-10 courses to reach 30 ECTS points. For me, i had to go to an exam in all of my courses. I had 9 exams/papers in a span of 3 weeks. Most of the students at SFU postpone exams to a "second try" a month later, but because i was going home i couldnt. 
Also, all of the written exams are with pen and paper.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The city of Vienna, with its culture and nature. Getting to know local people and other students from around the world. Getting away from my known sorroundings and out of my comfort zone.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge of my exchange stay was the academic frustration i experienced at SFU, as described above. Besides this, i found the city very liveable and with a lot of offers to socialize and experience culture and history. I would very much reccomend going abroad to Vienna!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: The above mentioned critique of SFU, might sound a little rough, but i was geniunly taken aback by the poor state of the university. The administration was overworked, and people where quiting there jobs (including our Erasmus coordinator and the main person at the Study Service Center), the academic level seemed (to me) to be equivalent to a high school level. The environment in class was characterized by talkin loudly and playing games, not paying respect to the teacher. But the teachers often didnt feel competent enough to communicate the academics in an appropriate way that corresponded to the level of the students.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
